name: BQ25601DRTWR
title: BQ25601D: I2C-controlled 3-A single-cell buck charger with NVDC power path, D+/D– USB source detection and USB OTG boost
summary: The BQ25601D charges one Li-ion or Li-polymer cell at up to 3 A from a 3.9 to 13.5 V input (22 V absolute) with a 1.5 MHz synchronous buck whose four power FETs (input blocking, high side, low side and battery FET) are all inside a 4 mm × 4 mm 24-pin WQFN. Its narrow-VDC power path holds the system rail at or above a programmable minimum (3.5 V default) so the load runs with a flat or missing battery, and tops the input up from the cell when the adapter runs short. A host sets charge voltage, currents, input limits, timers and the JEITA profile over I2C at address 6BH, but the part also charges on its own with default settings; it reads D+/D– to recognise SDP, DCP and several proprietary adapters, and runs in reverse as a 5.15 V, up to 1.2 A boost for USB On-The-Go. Ship mode, a push-button system reset on QON, thermistor monitoring, a safety timer and input, battery, system and thermal protection are built in.

pins.name: VBUS
pins.function: Charger input. The internal n-channel reverse-blocking FET (RBFET, Q1) sits between VBUS and PMID. A 1 µF ceramic from VBUS to GND goes near the chip.

pins.name: D+
pins.function: USB data line, positive side. Used for BC1.2 data-contact detection, primary and secondary detection, and for recognising non-standard adapters.

pins.name: D-
pins.function: USB data line, negative side (D–). Same detection role as D+.

pins.name: STAT
pins.function: Open-drain charge status. Low while charging; high when charging is complete or the charger sleeps; 1 Hz square wave at 50% duty on a charge-suspending fault. Pull up to a logic rail with 10 kΩ, or drive an LED through a current-limit resistor from a rail. EN_ICHG_MON[1:0] can turn the function off.

pins.name: SCL
pins.function: I2C clock. Pull up to the logic rail with 10 kΩ.

pins.name: SDA
pins.function: I2C data. Pull up to the logic rail with 10 kΩ.

pins.name: INT
pins.function: Open-drain interrupt, active low (INT with overbar). Gives a 256 µs low pulse to tell the host of a status change or fault. Pull up to a logic rail with 10 kΩ.

pins.name: NC
pins.function: No internal connection; leave floating.

pins.name: CE
pins.function: Charge enable, active low (CE with overbar). Charging is allowed while this pin is low.

pins.name: TS
pins.function: Battery temperature input for the JEITA profile. An NTC thermistor connects to this pin, with a divider from REGN to TS to GND setting the temperature window; charging stops when TS leaves the window. A 103AT-2 thermistor is the recommended type. Unused: 10 kΩ from REGN to TS and 10 kΩ from TS to GND.

pins.name: QON
pins.function: BATFET enable and reset input, active low (QON with overbar), with an internal pull-up. In ship mode, a low lasting tSHIPMODE turns the BATFET back on. With no VBUS, a low lasting tQON_RST (8 s minimum) switches the BATFET off for tBATFET_RST (250 ms minimum) and back on, a full power reset of SYS.

pins.name: BAT
pins.function: Battery positive terminal. The internal BATFET and current sensing lie between SYS and BAT. Place 10 µF close to the pin.

pins.name: SYS
pins.function: Converter output feeding the system. The internal current sensing sits between SYS and BAT. Place 20 µF close to the pin.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switching node, to the output inductor. The 0.047 µF bootstrap capacitor runs from SW to BTST.

pins.name: BTST
pins.function: Supply for the high-side gate driver; inside, it is the cathode of the bootstrap diode. The 0.047 µF bootstrap capacitor runs from SW to BTST.

pins.name: REGN
pins.function: Low-side gate drive and internal supply, from an internal LDO; inside, it is the anode of the bootstrap diode. Needs a 4.7 µF, 10 V ceramic to GND close to the chip. Also biases the TS divider and can be the STAT pull-up rail.

pins.name: PMID
pins.function: Node joining the drain of the reverse-blocking FET and the drain of the high-side FET. Needs a 10 µF ceramic to GND.

pins.name: VAC
pins.function: Input voltage sense for the charger. Must be tied to VBUS.

pins.name: PAD
pins.function: Exposed thermal pad: the chip's ground reference and its main heat path. Solder it to a ground plane with vias under the pad.

notes: Pin types: analog in, analog in/out, digital in, digital out, digital in/out, power.

circuits.title: Power path management application
circuits.description: The full charger around one BQ25601D for a 3.9 to 13.5 V input, 3 A input and charge current and a 4.2 V cell. VBUS and VAC share the input, with a TVS to ground and 1 µF on VBUS and 10 µF on PMID. The buck runs from SW through 1 µH into SYS, which carries two 10 µF capacitors and feeds the system at 3.5 to 4.6 V; 47 nF from SW to BTST is the bootstrap and 4.7 µF decouples REGN. The cell sits on BAT with 10 µF. The pack thermistor (10 kΩ) goes from TS to ground, with 5.23 kΩ from REGN and 30.1 kΩ to ground setting the TS window. SDA, SCL and INT each have 10 kΩ to the host's logic rail; CE goes to the host and D+/D– to the USB connector. An optional LED from SYS through 2.2 kΩ shows STAT, and an optional push button pulls QON to ground.

notes: Both NC pins (8 and 10) float.

operation.text: Four power switches are on chip: Q1, the reverse-blocking FET between VBUS and PMID; Q2, the high-side switch from PMID to SW; Q3, the low-side switch from SW to ground; and Q4, the battery FET between SYS and BAT. The bootstrap diode for the high-side driver is also inside.

Internal bias comes from whichever of VBUS and BAT is higher. Once VBUS passes its UVLO or BAT passes VBAT_UVLOZ, the sleep and battery-depletion comparators and the BATFET driver start, the I2C port answers, and every register holds its default.

With only a battery above VBAT_DPL_RISE, the BATFET connects it to SYS and REGN stays off to keep quiescent current low. Discharge current through the BATFET is watched all the time; above IBATFET_OCP the BATFET opens at once and BATFET_DIS is set, and it stays off until an input is plugged in or one of the ship-mode exit methods is used.

On plug-in the sequence is: REGN LDO on, poor-source check, D+/D– source detection setting the input current limit, VINDPM set-up, then the converter starts. REGN turns on when VAC is above VVAC_PRESENT, VAC exceeds VBAT + VSLEEPZ (buck) or VBUS is below VBAT + VSLEEP (boost), and a 220 ms delay has passed; otherwise the part sits in HIZ drawing under IVBUS_HIZ and the battery runs the system.

Before the buck starts, VBUS must be below VVAC_OV and must stay above VVBUSMIN while the chip sinks IBADSRC (30 mA typ). On passing, VBUS_GD is set and INT pulses. A source that fails is retried every 2 s.

After VBUS_GD, the D+/D– lines are run through BC1.2 detection (SDP, DCP) and, once the data-contact-detection timer runs out, a check of the fixed divider levels that some vendors' adapters put on D+ and D–. A DCP gets 2.4 A, an unknown adapter 0.5 A, and the divider types 1, 2, 2.1 or 2.4 A. When detection ends INT pulses, IINDPM is rewritten, PG_STAT is set and VBUS_STAT shows the source type. The host may overwrite IINDPM afterwards; IINDPM always caps the input current.

VINDPM can be set from 3.9 V to 5.4 V and defaults to 4.5 V. VDPM_BAT_TRACK[1:0] can make it follow the battery: the working limit is then the higher of the register value and VBAT plus 200, 250 or 300 mV.

When the input current limit is settled the buck starts switching; if charging is disabled the BATFET opens. Until SYS reaches 2.2 V the input current is held to the lower of 200 mA and IINDPM, then IINDPM alone applies. The buck runs at a fixed 1.5 MHz, moving to PFM at light load, below the minimum system voltage or with charging off. PFM_DIS stops PFM in buck and boost; PFM is only possible when IINDPM is 500 mA or more and is off at 400 mA or less.

The converter can run backwards from the battery to supply 5.15 V on VBUS, up to 1.2 A (BOOST_LIM), which covers the 500 mA USB OTG need. It starts when BAT is above VOTG_BAT, VBUS is below BAT + VSLEEP, OTG_CONFIG = 1, TS is between VBHOT and VBCOLD, and 30 ms have passed since enable. VBUS_STAT reads 111 meanwhile. Boost starts in PFM and then goes to PWM to keep overshoot down, and it keeps running while BAT stays above VOTG_BAT. Soft start limits inrush into loads up to 500 µF.

operation.topic: Host mode, default mode and watchdog
operation.text: After power-on reset the part is in default mode (watchdog expired, WATCHDOG_FAULT = 1) and charges on its own with default settings and a 10-hour fast-charge timer; when that ends charging stops but the buck keeps feeding the system. Writing WD_RST = 1 enters host mode. The host must then rewrite WD_RST before each watchdog period or set WATCHDOG = 00. If the watchdog runs out, the part goes back to default mode and resets every register to default; BATFET_DIS, BATFET_DLY, BATFET_RST_EN, VINDPM and IINDPM keep their values.

With CHG_CONFIG = 1 and CE low the part charges without host help. A cycle starts when the converter is running, charging is enabled with ICHG not 0 mA, TS and the safety timer show no fault, and BATFET_DIS = 0. It terminates when current is under ITERM and the battery is above the recharge threshold, provided the part is not in DPM or thermal regulation; when the cell later falls below the recharge threshold (VRECHG bit) a new cycle begins. Toggling CE or CHG_CONFIG also restarts charging. CHRG_STAT reports 00 not charging, 01 precharge, 10 fast charge (both the CC and CV phases), 11 done; INT pulses at completion.

Below 2.2 V the cell gets ISHORT (about 100 mA); from 2.2 V to 3 V the precharge current IPRECHG; above 3 V the fast-charge current ICHG, then constant voltage at VREG, with an optional top-off period. In input DPM or thermal regulation the real current is below the setting, termination is held off and the safety timer counts at half speed.

At termination the BATFET opens while the converter keeps powering SYS; the BATFET can close again for supplement mode. CHRG_STAT goes to 11 and INT pulses. Termination waits while the part is in input current, input voltage or thermal regulation, and EN_TERM = 0 turns it off. At low termination settings (25 to 50 mA) comparator offset can end the charge 10 to 20 mA above target, so a top-off timer (15, 30 or 45 min) can extend charging after termination; it follows the safety timer's suspension and doubling, reads its setting when termination is detected, and is reset by a charge enable, a new termination, or REG_RST. TOPOFF_ACTIVE shows it running, and INT pulses on entering and leaving it.

Charging only starts with TS between the T1 and T5 thresholds and stops outside them until the battery returns. Between T1 (0°C) and T2 (10°C) the charge current drops to 50% or 20% of ICHG (JEITA_ISET). Between T3 (45°C) and T5 (60°C) the charge voltage is either VREG or 4.1 V (JEITA_VSET). Termination is off in the cool and warm bands. Between T2 and T3 charging is normal.

In boost the battery must stay between VBCOLD (about –10°C to –20°C) and VBHOT (about 60°C to 65°C). Outside that window boost pauses, VBUS_STAT reads 000 and NTC_FAULT is set; boost resumes and the fault clears when the temperature comes back.

The timer allows 2 hours below VBATLOWV and 10 hours above it by default; CHG_TIMER selects 5 or 10 hours. On expiry CHRG_FAULT = 11 and INT pulses. EN_TIMER turns it off. During input voltage or current regulation, JEITA cool or thermal regulation it counts at half speed (so 5 hours becomes 10 in continuous IINDPM) unless TMR2X_EN = 0. It pauses during a fault and resets when charging is stopped and restarted with CE or CHG_CONFIG.

The BATFET separates SYS from the battery. Below the SYS_MIN setting the BATFET works as a linear regulator and SYS sits about 180 mV above the minimum; above it the BATFET is fully on and SYS is the battery voltage plus the BATFET drop. With charging off or terminated, SYS is held about 50 mV above the battery. VSYS_STAT is high during minimum-system-voltage regulation.

When the input reaches its current limit or falls to VINDPM, the charge current is cut back until both limits are respected. If the charge current has reached zero and the input is still overloaded, SYS sags below the battery and the BATFET turns on so the battery helps carry the load (supplement mode). VDPM_STAT or IDPM_STAT shows which limit is active.

The BATFET turns on when SYS falls 180 mV (battery above VSYSMIN) or 45 mV (battery below VSYSMIN) under BAT. At low current its gate is regulated to hold about 30 mV across it so the part does not bounce in and out of the mode; as current rises the gate drive increases until the FET is fully on, after which the drop rises linearly with current. It leaves supplement mode when the battery falls below the depletion threshold.

Setting BATFET_DIS opens the BATFET, either at once or after tSM_DLY (BATFET_DLY), so SYS is dead and battery drain is minimal. The BATFET comes back on when an adapter is plugged in, BATFET_DIS is cleared, REG_RST is set, or QON goes from high to low for longer than tSHIPMODE. Leaving ship mode through QON also sets EN_HIZ = 1; OTG cannot be enabled until the host clears it. With no input and BATFET_DIS = 0, holding QON low for tQON_RST opens the BATFET for tBATFET_RST and then closes it, giving the system a power-on reset; BATFET_RST_EN = 0 disables this.
PG_STAT goes high when VBUS is above its UVLO, above the battery, below VVAC_OV, holds above VVBUSMIN (3.8 V typ) while sinking IBADSRC (30 mA typ), and source detection is complete.

A 256 µs INT pulse is sent when a USB or adapter source is identified, a good input is found, the input is removed, charging completes, any REG09 fault occurs, or a VINDPM or IINDPM event happens (these two can be masked). A fault is latched in REG09 and no further fault INT is sent until the host reads it. Reading REG09 twice in a row gives first the latched faults, then the present state; NTC_FAULT always shows the live TS condition. REG09 cannot be part of a multi-byte read or write.
Above VVAC_OV (set by the OVP bits) switching stops immediately, CHRG_FAULT = 01 and INT pulses. Normal operation resumes by itself once the input falls back below the threshold.
During load transients SYS is clamped: when it is regulating at VSYSMIN, the SYSOVP trip is 350 mV above that level, switching stops at once, and a 30 mA sink pulls SYS back down.

The boost has accurate constant-current limiting. On a VBUS short it shuts down and retries 7 times; if that fails OTG_CONFIG is cleared, BOOST_FAULT is set and INT pulses, and re-enabling boost clears the fault. If VBUS rises above VOTG_OVP, switching stops, OTG_CONFIG is cleared, BOOST_FAULT is set and INT pulses.

In buck mode, above the thermal regulation limit (110°C default, 90°C selectable) the charge current is reduced; termination is then off, the safety timer runs at half speed and THERM_STAT is high. Above TSHUT (160°C) the converter and BATFET turn off, CHRG_FAULT reports it and INT pulses; both come back when the die cools by TSHUT_HYS (30°C). In boost mode thermal shutdown clears OTG_CONFIG and opens the BATFET; the BATFET recovers automatically when the die cools by 30°C, and the host may then re-enable OTG.

Battery overvoltage is 4% above the regulation voltage: charging stops at once, BAT_FAULT goes high and INT pulses. Below VBAT_DPL_FALL the BATFET opens to stop over-discharge, and only an input on VBUS recovers it; the cell is then charged at ISHORT (about 100 mA) below VSHORT, or at IPRECHG between VSHORTZ and VBAT_LOWV. A short or heavy overload of SYS beyond the BATFET current limit latches the BATFET off until one of the ship-mode exit events.

The part is an I2C slave at 7-bit address 6BH with registers REG00 to REG0B; reads past 0Bh return FFh, and an undefined register address is answered with NACK. Standard (100 kbit/s) and fast (400 kbit/s) modes are supported; SDA and SCL are open drain and need pull-ups. Single and multi-byte reads and writes are supported across REG00 to REG0B, except REG09.

Input: low-ESR X7R or X5R ceramic, placed right at the high-side drain and low-side source, rated above the input voltage (25 V or more for a 15 V input); 22 µF suits 3 A charging. Output: the internal compensation is set for 20 µF or less of ceramic capacitance; 10 V X7R or X5R parts are preferred.

To have a voltage on SYS the part needs an input of 3.9 V to 14.2 V able to deliver at least 100 mA on VBUS, and a single Li-ion cell above VBATUVLO on BAT. For full output power the source must supply at least 3 A.

Keep the high-frequency current loop small, in this order: input capacitor tight to PMID and GND; inductor right at SW, with a trace wide enough for the charge current but of minimum area, on one layer only and away from other copper; output capacitor close to the inductor and chip, grounded to the IC ground by a short path or plane. Run analog ground apart from power ground and join them only at the thermal pad (or through a 0 Ω resistor), right under the chip. Put decoupling capacitors at their pins. Solder the exposed pad to ground with enough thermal vias straight under the IC, and size vias for the currents they carry.

packages.name: RTW (S-PWQFN-N24), 24-pin WQFN, 0.5 mm pitch
notes: Dimensions in millimetres, toleranced to ASME Y14.5M-1994; the outline falls within JEDEC MO-220.
The exposed pad must be soldered to the board for heat and mechanical strength. Pin 1 corner is marked top and bottom; the pad may carry a chamfer at pin 1.
